Coram: Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 Oral Judgment

Aggrieved by the award passed in M.V.C.No.1731/2020 dated 27.12.2022 by the III Additional Judge and MACT of Small Causes, Bengaluru, the claimants are before this Court for seeking enhancement of the compensation.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.20,00,000/- for the death of the deceased.
2. Virtually, wife was claimant during the pendency of the petition.
Wife died and two daughters and son were impleaded as legal representatives.

The Court had granted the compensation as per the table given below:
 Sl. Compensation  Compensation heads  No. amount  1 Loss of dependency Rs. 5,80,000/-
 2 Loss of consortium Rs. 44,000/-
 3 Loss of estate Rs. 16,500/-
 Funeral and obsequies  4 Rs. 16,500/-
 ceremony expenses  5 Transportation of dead body Rs. 10,000/-
 6

Medical expenses Rs. 2,10,558/-
 Total Rs. 8,77,558/-
 NC: 2025:KHC:34679 HC-KAR
3. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants- claimants submits that under the head of loss of consortium, the amount that is awarded by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable.
He submits that the compensation needs to be enhanced.

Smt. Sarvamanagala vs Acko Gen.Ins. Co.Ltd on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158276728/
3
4. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent- Insurance Company submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.
6. The Tribunal under the head of loss of dependency had rightly granted Rs.5,80,000/-.
The wife died during the pendency of the petition.
The legal representatives i.e., 2 daughters and 1 son are entitled towards loss of consortium of an amount of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.44,000/- x 4).
Towards 'funeral expenses' an amount of Rs.36,000/- is granted and towards 'medical expenses' an amount of Rs.2,10,558/- is granted.
NC: 2025:KHC:34679 HC-KAR 7.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.Mekala Vs. M.
Malathi And Another1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards 'Legal Expenses'.
8.

Altogether, the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.10,12,558/-.
10.
Accordingly, the appeal of the claimants is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation from Rs.8,77,558/- to Rs.10,12,558/-.
i) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
ii) The respondent - Insurance Company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.
On such deposit, the claimants are entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iii) The apportionment of the compensation as per the award passed by the Tribunal.
iv) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.

v) The claimants are not entitled for interest for a period of 197 days.
 vi) No costs.
NC: 2025:KHC:34679 HC-KAR vii) Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
